subject: Interim endorsement request — Nexonix SOC 2 post-report gap
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@nexonix.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@nexonix.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: interim endorsement / bridge letter to cover post-report period

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the SOC 2 Type II that you provided during diligence. Nexonix is moving to finalize our security attestation for an upcoming vendor review. We have a gap between Redwood's SOC 2 report period (ended 2026-06-30) and our contract/go-live date. Our auditor has asked for an interim endorsement (often called a "bridge" letter) that affirms the controls in the report remain in place and that there have been no material changes since 2026-06-30 through today (we're hoping coverage through 2026-11-14).

Specifically we need:
- A short signed letter on Redwood letterhead referencing the SOC 2 Type II (report date and period) and stating the company is not aware of any material changes to the control environment since the report end date.
- Confirmation of any changes to encryption, KMS/HSM use, logical access, or third-party subprocessors since the report date (if none, a clear statement).
- Can the letter say it covers through 2026-11-14? If you require different language, please advise.

Please also confirm whether a scanned PDF signature is acceptable or if the letter must be executed via DocuSign. We need to send this to our auditor by 2026-11-20.

I've attached the SOC 2 you previously provided and our draft of the ask for your legal team to review (nexonix-bridge-letter-ask-20261110.pdf). Happy to hop on a short call if it's easier.

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Neill
Security Programs Lead
Nexonix
liam.oneill@nexonix.com

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear note and timeline. We're able to support an interim endorsement in most cases.

Quick clarifying Qs before we route to Legal:
- Is coverage through 2026-11-14 sufficient (you mentioned that date) or do you need "through the date of issuance" language?
- Are there any particular phrasing constraints from your auditor (we've seen stricter language for some FIs).

Cc'ing Soojin (InfoSec) and Rishi (GTM compliance) to confirm control-status and draft the letter. We'll aim to return a draft within 48–72 hours and confirm signature mechanism.

For transparency, I'll attach the SOC 2 we have on file and ask Soojin to include a short statement on any control changes. If there have been changes that materially affect a control, we will note them; otherwise we'll state none.

Subject: Draft: interim endorsement language for Nexonix (SOC 2)

Marissa / Rishi —

Below is my proposed language for the interim endorsement. I kept it concise to match auditor expectations; legal should review and we can convert to letterhead/pdf.

--- Proposed interim endorsement (draft) ---
Redwood Inference, Inc.
Date: November 13, 2026

To Whom It May Concern,

This letter is provided in connection with the SOC 2 Type II report issued by [Independent Auditor] for Redwood Inference, Inc., covering the period from January 1, 2026 through June 30, 2026 ("the Report"). Based on management's inquiry and the information available to us as of the date of this letter, Redwood Inference confirms that there have been no material changes to the control environment described in the Report that would materially affect the suitability of the design or operating effectiveness of the controls through November 14, 2026.

Specifically, Redwood confirms there have been no material modifications to:
- Encryption and key management practices (production KMS remains managed via our cloud provider and in-production keys are protected by customer-managed KMS/HSM where configured);
- Logical access controls, including SSO, role-based access, and privileged access reviews; and
- Subprocessor relationships relevant to the scope of the Report.

If you require additional detail on any control area (for example, a change-log or evidence package), please let us know and we will coordinate providing redacted supporting artifacts under an appropriate NDA.

Sincerely,

[Name]
[Title]
Redwood Inference, Inc.
---

Notes: 1) The language avoids asserting auditor opinions; we reference management inquiry and the date coverage. 2) We should confirm the KMS line if legal prefers less detail ("customer-managed KMS/HSM where configured" is intentionally conservative). 3) Attach the draft as bridge-letter-draft.docx for legal redline.

Attachments: bridge-letter-draft.docx

- Statement: no material changes to the control environment affecting the Report as of 2026-11-14.
- KMS/HSM and access-control language: included at a high level (no operational secrets or key material disclosed).

3) If your auditor requires additional artifacts (control change logs, redacted evidence), we'll coordinate delivery under NDA — let us know which control areas they want.

If everything looks good I'll mark this closed once DocuSign completes.
